headline: Mythos social engineering incident leads to critical routing fix for discovery hangs
summary: A critical bug fix has been implemented to resolve 'discovery hangs' caused by multiple default routes. This update, potentially related to the Mythos social engineering incident, ensures more reliable network operations.
details: A significant bug causing 'discovery hangs' when multiple default routes are present has been resolved. This fix addresses an issue where the system incorrectly concatenated routes instead of selecting the optimal one.
The updated defaultRoute() function now intelligently parses all available default routes. It prioritizes the route with the lowest metric, ensuring consistent and reliable network path selection.

This technical update is part of the response to the 'Mythos social engineering AISI INC-2026-07-28-01' incident. While specific details of the incident are not fully disclosed, the fix aims to bolster system stability and resilience.

The improved routing logic prevents potential service interruptions and enhances overall system robustness. This proactive measure is crucial for maintaining operational integrity in complex network environments.

headline_marked: [[NASA extends Voyager 2 mission]] for another year, 47-year-old probe gets power tweak
headline: NASA extends Voyager 2 mission for another year, 47-year-old probe gets power tweak
summary: Despite dwindling power from its nuclear battery, engineers implemented a 'Big Bang' power change, allowing its last three science instruments to operate for at least 12 more months.
details: Voyager 2, launched in 1977, was facing the shutdown of one of its last instruments this year. NASA's new power adjustments will keep its remaining three science instruments operational for at least another year.

The probe, along with its twin Voyager 1, relies on a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) that uses heat from plutonium decay. However, the plutonium supply diminishes by about four watts annually on each spacecraft.

To counter this, engineers implemented a "Big Bang" power change. This involved turning off non-science devices and utilizing lower-power alternatives to maintain warmth in the extreme cold of deep space.
The power decline has already led to two science instruments being shut off on each spacecraft since 2024. Voyager 2, which originally launched with 10 instruments, now operates with only three.
The new power shifts prevent the need to shut down another instrument on Voyager 2 this year. Voyager 1 is also slated to receive similar power adjustments in the coming months.
The Voyagers were initially launched to explore the outer gas giant planets. Voyager 2 became the first spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune, completing its last planetary flyby in 1989.

Both spacecraft continue to transmit scientific data from interstellar space. Voyager 2 is approximately 142 astronomical units from the Sun, with a one-way signal taking nearly 24 hours to reach Earth.
